_note: Issue 0 copy. Every sentence traces to a China Daily Brief item (Sep 28 to Oct 2, 2026) or the tracker. Editor's Note, Week at a Glance and Heard on the Hill are drafts for the comms coordinator to rewrite.
re_line: Trump-Xi summit's $30B tariff deal, Perdue's arms-offer disclosure, Senators press on Taiwan arms, Xi's National Day Taiwan line
editors_note: Good morning, and welcome to the first China Room Brief. It lands every Friday.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Beijing's fuel-export pause meets Golden Week's end
week_at_a_glance.body: China's holiday ends Oct 7, and Lianhe Zaobao reports it is unclear whether Beijing resumes fuel-export approvals after it.
week_at_a_glance.why: Reuters expects the suspension to tighten diesel and jet fuel across Asia.
bullets: Refiners suspended October exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau.
PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on Sep 30.
The New York Times ties the curbs to dwindling domestic inventories.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Greer's overcapacity move is due "within weeks"
week_at_a_glance.body: USTR Jamieson Greer told Nikkei the US will unveil countermeasures against overproduction from China, Japan and others "within weeks."
week_at_a_glance.why: The summit's tariff relief still has no start date. Greer said no timeline is set for cuts under the Board of Trade mechanism.
bullets: Reuters: the US has slowed aircraft-part exports to China to build leverage.
Greer's "Milwaukee framework" on steel excess capacity, agreed by the 28-member global steel forum, leaves China out (AFP).

week_at_a_glance.headline: Beijing's 1.2 trillion yuan injection lands Oct 8
week_at_a_glance.body: The PBOC's three-month reverse repo follows the mortgage-interest subsidy that took effect Oct 1.
week_at_a_glance.why: It is the first test of whether Beijing's "practical additional policies" reach the economy.
bullets: September manufacturing PMIs hit 50.1, ending two months of contraction.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senators press Trump on $14B Taiwan package
heard_on_the_hill.body: Twenty-one Democrats led by Jeanne Shaheen urged Trump to "immediately deliver congressionally approved defense assistance to Taiwan."
bullets: They cite $1.3 billion in appropriated funds and a $14 billion package approved nine months ago.
Four Republican senators separately called for its release.
Armed Services Chair Roger Wicker said US commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taipei's representative, Alexander Yui.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson: Taiwan arms aren't trade leverage
heard_on_the_hill.body: Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed suggestions the delayed package is a bargaining chip in trade talks.
bullets: He said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across two terms.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Chinese car ban slips past the midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate put off a bill permanently barring Chinese-made cars until after Nov 3, AP reported.
bullets: Reuters: senators plan a vote in November.
Sen. Bernie Moreno says his separate bill, aimed at automakers more than 15% Chinese-owned, won't touch Mercedes-Benz.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bipartisan bill targets Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senators from both parties proposed barring Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period.
heard_on_the_hill.why: Markets noticed. Shenzhen's ChiNext index fell 4.53% the next trading day.

in_the_news.headline: China, US agree to AI-incident channel, $30bn tariff cuts in eight-point summit consensus
in_the_news.body: Washington and Beijing agreed to an AI-incident channel and lower tariffs on $30 billion of goods each way.
in_the_news.why: It is the summit's main deliverable, set out in an eight-point readout that also promises a November AI dialogue.

in_the_news.headline: Trump asked Xi if China wanted to buy US weapons, ambassador says
in_the_news.body: Ambassador David Perdue says Trump asked Xi whether China wanted to buy American weapons. Trump says he "never heard of" it.
in_the_news.why: The State Department says the US has no plans to sell weapons to China.

in_the_news.headline: Xi marks 77th PRC anniversary with hardened Taiwan message
in_the_news.body: Xi said China will "resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking 'Taiwanese independence,'" Reuters reported.
in_the_news.why: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council says the phrasing is not new.

in_the_news.headline: US officials see Chinese invasion of Taiwan unlikely before 2028
in_the_news.body: US officials told Reuters Beijing is unlikely to use force against Taiwan before 2028, despite Xi's 2027 readiness order.
in_the_news.why: The PLA purge has left two of seven Central Military Commission members in active service.

in_the_news.headline: Beijing unveils mortgage subsidy, rate cut and 1.2 trillion yuan liquidity injection
in_the_news.body: Beijing rolled out a mortgage-interest subsidy, a PSL rate cut and a 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo set for Oct 8.
in_the_news.why: September manufacturing PMIs returned to expansion at 50.1.

research_roundup.headline: The Scope and Nature of the U.S.-China Competition
research_roundup.body: Michael J. Mazarr and colleagues open a multi-report study: "The United States can protect its interests and gain leverage against China without blowing up the relationship."

research_roundup.headline: What did the Trump-Xi summit actually accomplish?
research_roundup.body: Brookings scholars including Ryan Hass, Yun Sun, Susan Thornton and Mireya Solís on "what the visit reveals about the future trajectory of U.S.-China relations."

research_roundup.headline: What Actually Happened at the Xi-Trump Summit
research_roundup.body: Neil Thomas, Lizzi C. Lee, Lyle Morris and others: the summit launched an AI dialogue and left Taiwan and tech competition unresolved.

research_roundup.headline: Trump Had the Chance to Address U.S.-China AI Safety. He Threw Xi a Party Instead.
research_roundup.body: Jeffrey Prescott on "sobering risk and opulent inaction" on AI safety.

research_roundup.headline: A Trump-Xi Summit Scorecard
research_roundup.body: Bonnie Glaser scores the visit item by item.

research_roundup.headline: Why Trump Rolled Out the Red Carpet for Xi, and Why He Shouldn't Have
research_roundup.body: Dan Blumenthal and Ian Jones: the treatment tells allies "that they are irrelevant."
